Trump: Becton Dickinson agrees to invest $3B in US manufacturing, including $1B+ in Nebraska
U.S. medical technology company Becton Dickinson
agreed to invest $3B to bring the manufacturing of essential medical products to the United States, President Donald Trump said Monday in a post on Truth Social.
BD will invest more than $1B ⁠in Nebraska to ramp up production of numerous products, ​including needles ​made ⁠with American steel, Trump noted.

BD said it plans to invest $19 billion in the U.S. over several years across capital, operations, and supply-chain initiatives, including $3 billion to expand manufacturing at strategic sites nationwide. The company expects to increase domestic production of essential medical consumables by about 5 billion units annually, raising the share of such products supplied from within the U.S. to roughly 80%, according to a statement.
CSL strikes $1.55B lixudebart deal with Alentis for rare kidney and liver diseases

Lixudebart is currently being evaluated in the Phase 2 RENAL trial for AAV-RPGN, a rare autoimmune disease that can cause rapid kidney function loss and irreversible kidney damage.
Viatris to buy Pacira BioSciences in $1.65B deal
said they entered into a definitive agreement under which Viatris will acquire all outstanding shares of Pacira for $36.50 per share in cash, representing an aggregate equity value of $1.65B.
The transaction is expected to close by the end of 2026.
Upon completion of the transaction, Pacira will become a wholly owned subsidiary of Viatris, and Pacira's common stock will no longer be listed for trading on the Nasdaq Global Select Market.
The deal advances Viatris’ innovative medicines strategy, adding two patent-protected pain therapies- EXPAREL, for acute postsurgical pain, and ZILRETTA, for osteoarthritis knee pain.
Pacira generated approximately $746M in total revenue and ~$177M in adjusted EBITDA during the last twelve months ended June 30, 2026.
